Ossicles.fact: Several sources, including Eustachi and Casseri, attribute the discovery of the malleus and incus to the anatomist and philosopher Achillini.

Ossicles.subject: Women & Society
Ossicles.question: The first published description of the stapes came in Pedro Jimeno's Dialogus de re medica (_____) although it had been previously described in public lectures by Giovanni Filippo Ingrassia at the Uni
Ossicles.fact: The first published description of the stapes came in Pedro Jimeno's Dialogus de re medica (1549) although it had been previously described in public lectures by Giovanni Filippo Ingrassia at the University of Naples as early as 1546.

Ossicles.subject: Women & Society
Ossicles.question: The term ossicle derives from ossiculum, a diminutive of "bone" (_____: os; genitive ossis)
Ossicles.fact: The term ossicle derives from ossiculum, a diminutive of "bone" (Latin: os; genitive ossis). The malleus gets its name from Latin malleus, meaning "hammer", the incus gets its name from Latin incus meaning "anvil" from incudere meaning "to forge with a hammer", and the stapes gets its name from Modern Latin "stirrup", probably an alteration of Late Latin stapia related to stare "to stand" and pedem, an accusative of pes "foot", so called because the bone is shaped like a stirrup – this was an...

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The _____ was 5th–6th-century Germanic ethnic group.
Ostrogoths.fact: The Ostrogoths (Latin: Ostrogothi, Austrogothi) were a Roman-era Germanic people who, in the 5th and 6th centuries, set up one of the two major Gothic kingdoms within the Western Roman Empire.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodoric belonged to the Amal dynasty, which had gained power in _____ after the collapse of Attila's Hunnic empire
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodoric belonged to the Amal dynasty, which had gained power in Pannonia after the collapse of Attila's Hunnic empire.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: His reign marked the height of _____ power and stability in Italy
Ostrogoths.fact: They drew on large Gothic populations settled in the Balkans since the 4th century and rose to prominence under Theodoric the Great, who in 493 set up the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy after defeating Odoacer. His reign marked the height of Ostrogothic power and stability in Italy.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: In 535, _____ I launched the Gothic War (535–554), aiming to restore imperial authority in the West
Ostrogoths.fact: In 535, Emperor Justinian I launched the Gothic War (535–554), aiming to restore imperial authority in the West.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The protracted war devastated the peninsula, and the _____ state collapsed by 554
Ostrogoths.fact: The protracted war devastated the peninsula, and the Ostrogothic state collapsed by 554.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Survivors were absorbed into the _____, who established their own kingdom in Italy by 568
Ostrogoths.fact: Survivors were absorbed into the Lombards, who set up their own kingdom in Italy by 568.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Ancient sources often referred to them simply as "Goths," but modern scholarship distinguishes them as one of the two main branches of the Gothic peoples, alongside the _____
Ostrogoths.fact: Ancient sources often referred to them simply as "Goths," but modern scholarship distinguishes them as one of the two main branches of the Gothic peoples, alongside the Visigoths.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The Goths appear in Roman records starting in the third century, in the regions north of the _____ and Black Sea
Ostrogoths.fact: The Goths appear in Roman records starting in the third century, in the regions north of the Lower Danube and Black Sea.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: They competed for influence and Roman subsidies with peoples who had lived longer in the area, such as the Carpi, and various _____, and they contributed men to the Roman military
Ostrogoths.fact: They competed for influence and Roman subsidies with peoples who had lived longer in the area, such as the Carpi, and various Sarmatians, and they contributed men to the Roman military.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The dividing line between the _____ and the Greuthungi, was reported by Ammianus to be the Dniester River, and to the east of the Greuthungi were Alans living near the River Don
Ostrogoths.fact: By the third century, the Goths were already composed of sub-groups with their own names, because the Tervingi, who bordered on the Roman Empire and the Carpathian Mountains, were mentioned separately on at least one occasion. The dividing line between the Tervingi and the Greuthungi, was reported by Ammianus to be the Dniester River, and to the east of the Greuthungi were Alans living near the River Don.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Goths were a minority in all the places they lived within the Roman empire, and no _____ language or distinct Gothic ethnicity has survived
Ostrogoths.fact: Goths were a minority in all the places they lived within the Roman empire, and no Gothic language or distinct Gothic ethnicity has survived. On the other hand, the Gothic language texts the Ostrogothic kingdom helped preserve are the only eastern Germanic language with "continuous texts" surviving, and the earliest significant remnants of any Germanic language.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: According to the proposal of _____, this was originally a boastful tribal name meaning "Goths of the rising sun", or "Goths glorified by the rising sun"
Ostrogoths.fact: According to the proposal of Wolfram, this was originally a boastful tribal name meaning "Goths of the rising sun", or "Goths glorified by the rising sun".

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Among other _____ group names, however, they are associated with the Greuthungi
Ostrogoths.fact: On the other hand, the Gothic language texts the Ostrogothic kingdom helped preserve are the only eastern Germanic language with "continuous texts" surviving, and the earliest significant remnants of any Germanic language. Among other Gothic group names, however, they are associated with the Greuthungi.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: These words are traditionally edited by modern scholars to include well-known peoples: "Peuci, _____, Austrogoti, Tervingi, Visi, Gipedes, Celtae etiam et Eruli" (emphasis added)
Ostrogoths.fact: These words are traditionally edited by modern scholars to include well-known peoples: "Peuci, Grutungi, Austrogoti, Tervingi, Visi, Gipedes, Celtae etiam et Eruli" (emphasis added).

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The first record of a _____ sub-group acting in its own name, specifically the Tervingi, was dated from 291
Ostrogoths.fact: In the article for Emperor Claudius Gothicus (reigned 268–270), the following garbled list of "Scythian" peoples is given who had been conquered by the emperor when he earned his title "Gothicus": "peuci trutungi austorgoti uirtingi sigy pedes celtae etiam eruli". The first record of a Gothic sub-group acting in its own name, specifically the Tervingi, was dated from 291.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The Greuthungi, Vesi, and _____ are all attested no earlier than 388
Ostrogoths.fact: The Greuthungi, Vesi, and Ostrogothi are all attested no earlier than 388.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Much later _____ also described Tribigild and his rebellion against the eunuch consul Eutropius
Ostrogoths.fact: Much later Zosimus also described Tribigild and his rebellion against the eunuch consul Eutropius. Zosimus believed that was conspiracy between the two Goths from the beginning.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Gainas, the aggrieved _____ general sent to fight Tribigild, openly joined forces with him after the death of Eutropius
Ostrogoths.fact: Gainas, the aggrieved Gothic general sent to fight Tribigild, openly joined forces with him after the death of Eutropius. Starting with the 6th century writer Jordanes, whose Getica is a history of the Ostrogothic Amal dynasty, there is a tradition of simply equating the Greuthungi with the Ostrogothi.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Zosimus believed that was conspiracy between the two _____ from the beginning
Ostrogoths.fact: Claudian only uses the term Ostrogoth once in the long poem, but in other references to this same group he more often calls them Greuthungi or "Getic" (an older word used poetically for Goths in this period). Zosimus believed that was conspiracy between the two Goths from the beginning.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Starting with the 6th century writer _____, whose Getica is a history of the Ostrogothic Amal dynasty, there is a tradition of simply equating the Greuthungi with the Ostrogothi
Ostrogoths.fact: Starting with the 6th century writer Jordanes, whose Getica is a history of the Ostrogothic Amal dynasty, there is a tradition of simply equating the Greuthungi with the Ostrogothi. Jordanes does not mention the Greuthungi at all by that name, but he identified the Ostrogothic kings of Italy, the Amal dynasty, as the heirs and descendants of king Ermanaric.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Jordanes does not mention the _____ at all by that name, but he identified the Ostrogothic kings of Italy, the Amal dynasty, as the heirs and descendants of king Ermanaric
Ostrogoths.fact: It is generally believed by historians that this Phrygian settlement of Greuthingi, called including Ostrogoths, were part of the Greuthungi-led force led by Odotheus in 386, and not the Greuthungi who had entered the empire earlier, in 376 under Alatheus and Saphrax. Starting with the 6th century writer Jordanes, whose Getica is a history of the Ostrogothic Amal dynasty, there is a tradition of simply equating the Greuthungi with the Ostrogothi.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: According to _____, the terms "Vesi" and "Ostrogothi" were used by the peoples themselves to boastfully describe themselves, and thus remained in use
Ostrogoths.fact: Modern historians agree that Jordanes is unreliable, especially for events long before his time, but some historians such as Herwig Wolfram defend the equation of the Greuthungi and Ostrogoths. Wolfram follows the position of Franz Altheim that the terms Tervingi and Greuthungi were older geographical identifiers used by outsiders to describe these Visigoths and Ostrogoths before they crossed the Danube, and that this terminology dropped out of use around 400, when many Goths had moved into t...

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: In any case, the older terminology of a divided Gothic people disappeared gradually after they entered the _____
Ostrogoths.fact: In any case, the older terminology of a divided Gothic people disappeared gradually after they entered the Roman Empire.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The term "_____" was an invention of the sixth century
Ostrogoths.fact: The term "Visigoth" was an invention of the sixth century. Cassiodorus, a Roman in the service of Theodoric the Great, invented the term Visigothi to match Ostrogothi, differentiating between "western Goths" and "eastern Goths" respectively.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Cassiodorus, a Roman in the service of _____ the Great, invented the term Visigothi to match Ostrogothi, differentiating between "western Goths" and "eastern Goths" respectively
Ostrogoths.fact: Cassiodorus, a Roman in the service of Theodoric the Great, invented the term Visigothi to match Ostrogothi, differentiating between "western Goths" and "eastern Goths" respectively.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: This usage, however, was adopted by the _____ themselves in their communications with the Byzantine Empire and was in use in the seventh century
Ostrogoths.fact: Furthermore, Cassiodorus used the term "Goths" to refer only to the Ostrogoths, whom he served, and reserved the geographical term "Visigoths" for the Gallo-Hispanic Goths. This usage, however, was adopted by the Visigoths themselves in their communications with the Byzantine Empire and was in use in the seventh century.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Other names for the _____ abounded
Ostrogoths.fact: Furthermore, Cassiodorus used the term "Goths" to refer only to the Ostrogoths, whom he served, and reserved the geographical term "Visigoths" for the Gallo-Hispanic Goths. This usage, however, was adopted by the Visigoths themselves in their communications with the Byzantine Empire and was in use in the seventh century.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: A "_____" Byzantine or Italian author referred to one of the two peoples as the Valagothi, meaning "Roman [walha] Goths"
Ostrogoths.fact: A "Germanic" Byzantine or Italian author referred to one of the two peoples as the Valagothi, meaning "Roman [walha] Goths".

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: This terminology survived in the _____ as late as the reign of Athalaric, who was called του Ουαλεμεριακου (tou Oualemeriakou) by John Malalas
Ostrogoths.fact: This terminology survived in the Byzantine East as late as the reign of Athalaric, who was called του Ουαλεμεριακου (tou Oualemeriakou) by John Malalas.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Many Greuthungi entered the _____ in 376 with Saphrax and Alatheus, and many of these Goths probably subsequently joined Alaric, contributing to the formation of the Visigothic kingdom
Ostrogoths.fact: Many Greuthungi entered the Roman Empire in 376 with Saphrax and Alatheus, and many of these Goths probably subsequently joined Alaric, contributing to the formation of the Visigothic kingdom.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The second major component of the Amal kingdom's population were the _____
Ostrogoths.fact: The second major component of the Amal kingdom's population were the Thracian Goths.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Valamir, the uncle of _____ the Great, is even depicted as Attila's most highly valued leader along with Ardaric of the Gepids
Ostrogoths.fact: Valamir, the uncle of Theodoric the Great, is even depicted as Attila's most highly valued leader along with Ardaric of the Gepids.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Modern historians such as _____ believe this is an exaggeration, and point out that there were at least three factions of Goths in Attila's forces
Ostrogoths.fact: Modern historians such as Peter Heather believe this is an exaggeration, and point out that there were at least three factions of Goths in Attila's forces.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodemir, father of _____, brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodemir, father of Theoderic, brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474. The younger uncle of Theoderic, Vidimir, with his like-named son and some of the Pannonian Goths, headed to Italy and his son was eventually settled in Gaul.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The younger uncle of _____, Vidimir, with his like-named son and some of the Pannonian Goths, headed to Italy and his son was eventually settled in Gaul
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodemir, father of Theoderic, brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474. The younger uncle of Theoderic, Vidimir, with his like-named son and some of the Pannonian Goths, headed to Italy and his son was eventually settled in Gaul.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodemir and _____ moved their Goths around the Balkans, while in the meantime, the Thracian Goths were the main focus of Gothic power
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodemir, father of Theoderic, brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474. The younger uncle of Theoderic, Vidimir, with his like-named son and some of the Pannonian Goths, headed to Italy and his son was eventually settled in Gaul.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: For some time they held a part of _____, controlling part of the Via Egnatia between the major Roman cities of Durrës and Thessalonika
Ostrogoths.fact: For some time they held a part of Macedonia, controlling part of the Via Egnatia between the major Roman cities of Durrës and Thessalonika.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodemir died in _____ in 474, having made sure that Theoderic (the future "Great") was designated as successor
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodemir died in Cyrrhus in 474, having made sure that Theoderic (the future "Great") was designated as successor.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: In the same year, the other _____ ("Strabo"), fell out of favour with the new emperor Zeno
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodemir and Theoderic moved their Goths around the Balkans, while in the meantime, the Thracian Goths were the main focus of Gothic power. Theodemir died in Cyrrhus in 474, having made sure that Theoderic (the future "Great") was designated as successor.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Wolfram has proposed that _____ was an Amal, whose father had split with Theoderic's branch only as recently as the time of the Battle of Nadao
Ostrogoths.fact: Wolfram has proposed that Theoderic Strabo was an Amal, whose father had split with Theoderic's branch only as recently as the time of the Battle of Nadao. Theoderic Strabo led a revolt in 473 and was declared king of the Goths.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: They formed a military force that was loyal to Aspar, the _____ magister militum ("master of soldiers") of Alanic-Gothic descent, who was killed in 471
Ostrogoths.fact: They formed a military force that was loyal to Aspar, the East Roman magister militum ("master of soldiers") of Alanic-Gothic descent, who was killed in 471. Aspar's death saw a change in the East Roman approach to Gothic military forces that he had been allied to.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Aspar's death saw a change in the _____ approach to Gothic military forces that he had been allied to
Ostrogoths.fact: They formed a military force that was loyal to Aspar, the East Roman magister militum ("master of soldiers") of Alanic-Gothic descent, who was killed in 471. Aspar's death saw a change in the East Roman approach to Gothic military forces that he had been allied to.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theoderic Strabo led a revolt in 473 and was declared king of the _____
Ostrogoths.fact: Theoderic Strabo led a revolt in 473 and was declared king of the Goths.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: As Wolfram noted, "His elevation as king in Thrace in 473 parallels the elevation of _____ in 476
Ostrogoths.fact: As Wolfram noted, "His elevation as king in Thrace in 473 parallels the elevation of Odoacer in 476.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: [...] A _____ federate army sought to force through its demands by making its general king"
Ostrogoths.fact: Aspar's death saw a change in the East Roman approach to Gothic military forces that he had been allied to. [...] A Roman federate army sought to force through its demands by making its general king".

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: The younger _____, son of Theodemir, was able to benefit from this
Ostrogoths.fact: With the death of Emperor Leo II, and the succession of Aspar's old rival Emperor Zeno in 474, the situation for the old Gothic party became increasingly difficult in the eastern empire, and Theoderic Strabo lost the support of the emperor. The younger Theoderic, son of Theodemir, was able to benefit from this.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: His kingdom, now based on the _____ in Moesia, was recognized as a federate kingdom and granted (at least in theory) an annual subsidy
Ostrogoths.fact: His kingdom, now based on the Lower Danube in Moesia, was recognized as a federate kingdom and granted (at least in theory) an annual subsidy.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: However, when Zeno forced the two Gothic groups into a confrontation in 478, _____ petitioned the Amal-led Goths, making a case for Gothic unity
Ostrogoths.fact: However, when Zeno forced the two Gothic groups into a confrontation in 478, Theoderic Strabo petitioned the Amal-led Goths, making a case for Gothic unity.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Strabo also appealed to Zeno, but Zeno made new offers to _____ the Amal instead, but these were rejected
Ostrogoths.fact: However, when Zeno forced the two Gothic groups into a confrontation in 478, Theoderic Strabo petitioned the Amal-led Goths, making a case for Gothic unity. Strabo also appealed to Zeno, but Zeno made new offers to Theoderic the Amal instead, but these were rejected.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Warfare between the Goths and imperial forces ensued, and the Amal-led Goths once again became mobile, leaving _____
Ostrogoths.fact: His kingdom, now based on the Lower Danube in Moesia, was recognized as a federate kingdom and granted (at least in theory) an annual subsidy. Warfare between the Goths and imperial forces ensued, and the Amal-led Goths once again became mobile, leaving Moesia.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Zeno proposed a new federate kingdom for them in Dacia, north of the _____, but instead the Goths attempted to take Durrës; however, Roman forces quickly repulsed them
Ostrogoths.fact: Zeno proposed a new federate kingdom for them in Dacia, north of the Danube, but instead the Goths attempted to take Durrës; however, Roman forces quickly repulsed them.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Between 479 and 481, it was the _____ under Theoderic Strabo who kept the Romans occupied, but in 481 Strabo died, when he fell from his horse and was impaled on a lance
Ostrogoths.fact: Between 479 and 481, it was the Thracian Goths under Theoderic Strabo who kept the Romans occupied, but in 481 Strabo died, when he fell from his horse and was impaled on a lance.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society

Ostrogoths.fact: His son Recitac was unable to retain Gothic support and was killed in 484 under orders from Theoderic the Amal, who united the two Gothic groups.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Zeno was forced to conclude a treaty and _____ the Amal was named consul in 484
Ostrogoths.fact: Between 479 and 481, it was the Thracian Goths under Theoderic Strabo who kept the Romans occupied, but in 481 Strabo died, when he fell from his horse and was impaled on a lance. His son Recitac was unable to retain Gothic support and was killed in 484 under orders from Theoderic the Amal, who united the two Gothic groups.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Hostilities between _____ the Amal's Goths and the Eastern Roman Empire began again by 487
Ostrogoths.fact: Between 479 and 481, it was the Thracian Goths under Theoderic Strabo who kept the Romans occupied, but in 481 Strabo died, when he fell from his horse and was impaled on a lance. His son Recitac was unable to retain Gothic support and was killed in 484 under orders from Theoderic the Amal, who united the two Gothic groups.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: His childhood was spent at _____ as a diplomatic hostage, where he was carefully educated
Ostrogoths.fact: His childhood was spent at Constantinople as a diplomatic hostage, where he was carefully educated.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodoric the Great, as he is sometimes distinguished, was sometimes the friend, sometimes the enemy, of the _____
Ostrogoths.fact: The early part of his life was taken up with various disputes, intrigues and wars within the Byzantine empire, in which he had as his rival Theodoric Strabo of the Thracian Goths, a distant relative of Theodoric the Great and son of Triarius. This older but lesser Theodoric seems to have been the chief, not the king, of that branch of the Ostrogoths that had settled within the Empire earlier.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: In the former case he was clothed with various Roman titles and offices, as patrician and consul; but in all cases alike he remained the national _____ king
Ostrogoths.fact: In the former case he was clothed with various Roman titles and offices, as patrician and consul; but in all cases alike he remained the national Ostrogothic king.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodoric is also known for his attainment of support from the _____ and on one occasion, he even helped resolve a disputed papal election
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodoric is also known for his attainment of support from the Catholic Church and on one occasion, he even helped resolve a disputed papal election.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: During his reign, _____, who was an Arian, allowed freedom of religion, which had not been done before
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodoric the Great, as he is sometimes distinguished, was sometimes the friend, sometimes the enemy, of the Empire. Theodoric is also known for his attainment of support from the Catholic Church and on one occasion, he even helped resolve a disputed papal election.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: However, he did try to appease the _____ and tried to keep his alliance with the church strong
Ostrogoths.fact: However, he did try to appease the Pope and tried to keep his alliance with the church strong. He saw the Pope as an authority not only in the church but also over Rome itself.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: He saw the _____ as an authority not only in the church but also over Rome itself
Ostrogoths.fact: However, he did try to appease the Pope and tried to keep his alliance with the church strong. He saw the Pope as an authority not only in the church but also over Rome itself.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: His ability to work well with Italy's nobles, members of the _____, and the Catholic Church all helped facilitate his acceptance as the ruler of Italy
Ostrogoths.fact: His ability to work well with Italy's nobles, members of the Roman Senate, and the Catholic Church all helped facilitate his acceptance as the ruler of Italy.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodoric sought to revive Roman culture and government and in doing so, profited the _____ people
Ostrogoths.fact: Theodoric sought to revive Roman culture and government and in doing so, profited the Italian people.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: It was in both characters together that he set out in 488, by commission from the _____ emperor Zeno, to recover Italy from Odoacer
Ostrogoths.fact: It was in both characters together that he set out in 488, by commission from the Byzantine emperor Zeno, to recover Italy from Odoacer.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: By 493 _____ was taken, where Theodoric would set up his capital

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: After entering _____ in 493, Theodoric refrained from adopting the title rex Gotorum, and instead assumed the posture of a Roman ruler
Ostrogoths.fact: By 493 Ravenna was taken, where Theodoric would set up his capital. After entering Ravenna in 493, Theodoric refrained from adopting the title rex Gotorum, and instead assumed the posture of a Roman ruler.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: It was also at this time that _____ was killed by Theodoric's own hand
Ostrogoths.fact: It was in both characters together that he set out in 488, by commission from the Byzantine emperor Zeno, to recover Italy from Odoacer. It was also at this time that Odoacer was killed by Theodoric's own hand.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Historian Ian Wood claims that _____'s reign in Italy following the fall of Odoacer reflected not a rupture from Roman traditions but their strategic appropriation
Ostrogoths.fact: By 493 Ravenna was taken, where Theodoric would set up his capital. It was also at this time that Odoacer was killed by Theodoric's own hand.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society

Ostrogoths.fact: In 498, the Eastern emperor Anastasius formally returned the imperial regalia to the West and allowed Theodoric to appoint consuls, effectively granting him symbolic seniority in the imperial hierarchy.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Rather than a distinctly "_____" regime, his court continued to function within the idioms of Roman law, ceremony, and governance
Ostrogoths.fact: Rather than a distinctly "Gothic" regime, his court continued to function within the idioms of Roman law, ceremony, and governance. Ostrogothic power was fully set up over Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia and the lands to the north of Italy.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Ostrogothic power was fully established over Italy, Sicily, _____ and the lands to the north of Italy
Ostrogoths.fact: Ostrogothic power was fully set up over Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia and the lands to the north of Italy.

Ostrogoths.subject: Women & Society
Ostrogoths.question: Theodoric forged alliances with the _____, Alamanni, Franks and Burgundians, some of which were accomplished through diplomatic marriages
